enriched_entities.name: neurofibromin 1
enriched_entities.function: Stimulates the GTPase activity of Ras. NF1 shows greater affinity for Ras GAP, but lower specific activity. May be a regulator of Ras activity. Functions as a negative regulator of RAS/MAPK signaling.
enriched_entities.disease_association: Loss-of-function mutations in NF1 cause Neurofibromatosis Type 1, leading to constitutive RAS activation

enriched_entities.name: DNA topoisomerase II alpha
enriched_entities.function: Controls and alters the topologic states of DNA during transcription. Catalyzes the transient breaking and rejoining of DNA strands to relieve tension and enable DNA replication and transcription. Primary molecular target of anthracyclines including doxorubicin.
enriched_entities.drug_target_relationship: Direct target of doxorubicin - TOP2A inhibition leads to DNA damage and apoptosis in cancer cells

enriched_entities.name: DNA topoisomerase II beta
enriched_entities.function: Controls and alters the topologic states of DNA during transcription. Unlike TOP2A, TOP2B is constitutively expressed and not cell cycle-dependent. Implicated in doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity.
enriched_entities.drug_target_relationship: TOP2B inhibition by doxorubicin in cardiomyocytes contributes to cardiotoxicity through mitochondrial dysfunction and DNA damage

enriched_entities.name: ATP binding cassette subfamily B member 1
enriched_entities.function: Energy-dependent efflux pump responsible for multidrug resistance. Exports various substrates across cell membranes including anticancer drugs like doxorubicin, reducing intracellular drug accumulation.
enriched_entities.drug_target_relationship: Overexpression of ABCB1 confers doxorubicin resistance by actively pumping drug out of cells

enriched_entities.name: ATP binding cassette subfamily C member 1
enriched_entities.function: Multispecific organic anion transporter that confers resistance to anticancer drugs. Mediates ATP-dependent export of organic anions and drug conjugates.
enriched_entities.drug_target_relationship: ABCC1 exports doxorubicin and its conjugates, reducing intracellular drug concentration and conferring resistance

enriched_entities.name: superoxide dismutase 2
enriched_entities.function: Mitochondrial enzyme that destroys superoxide radicals normally produced within cells. Critical for protection against oxidative stress. Cardioprotective against anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity.
enriched_entities.drug_target_relationship: SOD2 protects cardiomyocytes from doxorubicin-induced oxidative damage; genetic variants or reduced expression associated with increased cardiotoxicity risk

enriched_entities.name: glutathione peroxidase 1
enriched_entities.function: Protects cells from oxidative damage by catalyzing the reduction of hydrogen peroxide and lipid peroxides using glutathione. Major antioxidant enzyme in cardiovascular system.
enriched_entities.drug_target_relationship: GPX1 reduces doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity by neutralizing reactive oxygen species; lower activity correlates with increased cardiac damage

enriched_entities.name: catalase
enriched_entities.function: Catalyzes the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen. Key enzyme in cellular protection against oxidative stress. Provides cardioprotection against anthracycline toxicity.
enriched_entities.drug_target_relationship: Catalase provides cardioprotection by degrading H2O2 generated during doxorubicin metabolism, reducing oxidative cardiac injury

enriched_entities.name: tumor protein p53
enriched_entities.function: Tumor suppressor that regulates cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, senescence, DNA repair, and metabolism in response to cellular stress. Critical mediator of DNA damage response to genotoxic agents like doxorubicin.
enriched_entities.drug_target_relationship: TP53 mediates doxorubicin-induced apoptosis in cancer cells through DNA damage signaling; TP53 mutations common in resistant tumors

enriched_entities.name: ATM serine/threonine kinase
enriched_entities.function: Serine/threonine protein kinase that recruits and activates key proteins in DNA damage response, including p53. Central coordinator of cellular response to DNA double-strand breaks induced by genotoxic agents.
enriched_entities.drug_target_relationship: ATM senses doxorubicin-induced DNA damage and activates cell cycle checkpoints and apoptosis; ATM status affects tumor sensitivity to anthracyclines

drug.name: DOXORUBICIN
drug.mechanism: Topoisomerase II (TOP2A/TOP2B) poison that intercalates DNA and stabilizes TOP2-DNA cleavage complexes, leading to DNA double-strand breaks, cell cycle arrest, and apoptosis. Also generates reactive oxygen species through redox cycling.
drug.major_toxicity: Cardiotoxicity (dose-limiting), mediated by TOP2B inhibition in cardiomyocytes and oxidative stress

disease.name: Neurofibromatosis type 1
disease.description: Autosomal dominant tumor predisposition syndrome caused by loss-of-function mutations in the NF1 gene. Characterized by café-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, optic pathway gliomas, and increased risk of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs) and other cancers.
disease.pathophysiology: Loss of neurofibromin (NF1 protein) function impairs RAS-GTPase activity, leading to constitutive RAS/MAPK pathway activation, increased cell proliferation, and tumor formation.
disease.cancer_risk: Increased risk of benign and malignant tumors including neurofibromas, MPNSTs, gliomas, pheochromocytomas, and myeloid leukemias
disease.treatment_context: Doxorubicin may be used in chemotherapy regimens for NF1-associated malignancies such as MPNSTs and aggressive gliomas
